Ay, hijo, you make me laugh. Twenty-one P for the Mercado de la Paz — and that is my last word, cariño. If you say no, I put her back in the box and we talk about football instead. Have you eaten today?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one — Mercado de San Ildefonso, very pretty card, twenty-nine P. My late husband loved that market, we bought olives there every Sunday. It is a good one to start your album, hijo.
Venga, 25 P. You drive a hard bargain for someone so young!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look here — this is my Mercado de la Paz page, complete, all of it together. Very pretty, no? For you, twenty-nine. My grandson filled one just like it.

Hola, cariño, qué prisa llevas. ¿Has comido ya? Siéntate un momentito, el Rastro no se va a ninguna parte. Mira, el Neighbourhood pack lo tengo en 30. Es bonito, viene bien para empezar, muchos niños han empezado con ése en mi mesa.
Look, 25 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, cariño, you have a silver tongue! But the pack... 24 P, and that is me being soft. Have you eaten today? You look thin. Save a coin or two for your swaps — that page will fill faster than you think, hijo.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué prisa llevas, hijo. ¿Has comido ya? Mira, el Neighbourhood pack te lo dejo en 30 P. Es bonito, tiene cartas para empezar bien. Mi nieto empezó con uno igual, hace años, aquí mismo en esta mesita. Anda, llévatelo.
Ay, hijo, welcome, welcome. But that one, the CHA? Come back later. Have you eaten something today?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Mercado de la Paz, very pretty card, yours for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

payload.name: El Chato
payload.teaser: «Better packs, friendly prices. If I like you.»
payload.how: Better packs and rare singles; he buys uncommon and rare cards. Open a thread with him (with: chato).

payload.text: Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P.

Ay, está bien, hijo — twenty-three, it is yours. Take it with my blessing. Keep it flat in your bag, no bends, eh? My grandson still has his. Now go eat something, cariño, you look hungry. Come back Sunday and tell me how it looks.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong today. Have you eaten? Look, this one is my Neighbourhood pack, very good for starting — thirty P. My Pablo started with the same one, and now he beats his father. Take your time, hijo.

Ay, hijo, grandchildren already? Look — 23 P, and not one word more about it. Go eat something, por favor. And keep swapping those duplicates; a full page is worth much more than loose cards, cariño. You will see.

Ay, hijo, qué prisas. Mira, te lo dejo en 26, porque me caes bien. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. Cambia tus repetidas con los otros niños, ya verás. ¿Seguro que has comido algo hoy?
Look, 26 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. La Chulapa. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or keep walking.
Soy El Chato. Carmen está al lado. Teatro Valle-Inclán, treinta y tres primas. Ahí empezamos.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson! Look — 24 P, and I wrap it nice for you. Mercado de la Paz, it sits lovely on a page. Bring me your duplicates next Sunday, we find you the missing ones. Have you eaten something today, cariño?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — this one, Mercado de San Ildefonso, a beautiful card, my favourite colours. Twenty-nine P and it is yours, hijo. Forty years I sit here, and this one always makes people smile.

Ay, hijo, a churro — good, eat! But this is my last word: 22 P for the sobre_barrio. If no, we leave it, and still I smile at you next Sunday. Go on now, swap those duplicates — a full page is worth much more, cariño.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Taxi Blanco, a beautiful card, very good for starting a collection. For you, twelve P. My hands have passed this table forty years, and I still love seeing a new collector begin.
Mercado de la Paz. 13 P. Take it or leave it.
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Mercado de la Paz for 12 P. A good start for your album. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 24 P.
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
You move, I move. 33 P.
La Tabacalera. Thirty-three. You've been dealing straight with Carmen, so I'm showing you the good one first.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, hijo, you are too generous with me! But no, let us say 13 P and we are both happy. A fair little price for a pretty card. Take it, and go eat something warm, sí? Then come back and show me your album.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Still Chato. Still 33 P. You moved two, I moved nothing. That's how it works.
I'm not Abuela. Chato. Mercado de la Paz, 13 P. Same as before. House market takes five per cent — some teams run cheaper. Look around.
Three points. That is your big move? Thirty-three. Still thirty-three. Come back when you are serious, chaval.
Oh, oh... 26 P, and only because you have a kind face.

¡Hola, cariño! ¿Has comido ya? Qué bueno verte por aquí. Mira, el Puesto del Rastro te lo dejo en 5 primas, hijo, para que empieces con alegría. Y esta noche a las nueve y media abre El Chato, el de al lado; le gusta la gente que trata derecho.

¡Ay, hijo, you bargain like my own nieto! Ten P, and we shake hands, sí? And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates with your friends. Now go, eat something before the stalls close.

Ay, cariño, you say eighteen like a little song! But my price stays: 24 P, and I wrap it nice with paper. Mercado de la Paz, muy bonita. Bring duplicates next Sunday, we fill your page together. Now go eat something, hijo, you look hungry.
You again. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. Ninety-seven. Card speaks for itself.

Ay, cariño, such sweet words! But I cannot take so much from you. Fourteen P, and the Mercado de la Paz is yours. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, sí? And remember — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more.
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face. Eh, eh. Be nice to your abuela. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
No. 32 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You're Carmen's friend. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, 97 P.

Ay, hijo, you have a good heart. Twenty-three primas and the Samosas de la Plaza are yours. Have you eaten today? And listen — El Chato next door opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight, like you.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my Pablo! 24 P, and I put in a little duplicate for you — a card means nothing to me, but to you, maybe it finishes a page. Eat something, sí? And remember El Chato opens at half past nine.
¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Sit a moment. Yes, yes, it is a pretty card, kept with cariño, I see it. For the Taxi Blanco I can give you 5. That is my offer, hijo. Take your time thinking.
Mercado de San Ildefonso. 13 P. Take it or leave it.
Thirty-three. You move, I move. You haven't moved much.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué alegría verte. Have you eaten something today? Look, this one is La Galería — bonita, no? For you, 17 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
You move, I move. 33 P.
Three primas. That's your move? 97 P. Card's selling fine without you.
Silver pack. One eighty-eight. Abuela says you deal straight, so that's the price.

Hijo, mírame — asking the same thing five times does not change my price. That little trick, not with your abuela. 24 P, and I wrap it nice. Remember: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, cariño.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my Manolo. Ten P, and I wrap it nice for you, sí? That card wants a good home, and you have good eyes. Take it, go eat something warm, and come see me next Sunday with your duplicates.

Ay, qué cariño tienes, hijo. Mira — 25 P, and I wrap it nice for you. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Have you eaten? There is bread here if you want.
Ay hijo, you are kind, but 5 is what I can give for the Taxi Blanco. Still 5, cariño. Look, the little ones come Sunday with coins in their hands, you know? Sit, rest. Think slowly, no hurry with me.

Ay, hijo, qué detalle traerme un repetido. Guárdalo bien: una página completa vale mucho más que los cromos sueltos, así que cambia tus repes, cariño. El Puesto del Rastro te lo dejo en 6 primas, y tan amigos. ¿Has comido algo ya?
Sobres de barrio? No. Not here. Abuela handles those. I deal silver and singles.
Your abuela would've moved more than one. 31 P. I match what you move, nothing extra.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. Cine Doré. Ninety-seven. That's the number.
Three again. Fine. 96 P. I move like you move.
Abuela sent you. Bueno. Cine Doré, ninety-seven P. Good card. You want it or you want to stand there?
Still 13 P. You moved, I didn't. That's how it goes.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? Look, this one is La Galería, very pretty, twenty-nine P. A little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with your friends. They cost you nothing, no?

Ay, cariño, you talk so sweetly, but my hands are small ones. For the Taxi Blanco, 5. Still 5, hijo. And listen, a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Have you eaten? Sit, no hurry.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Mercado de la Paz, 29 P. Made for beginners.
Thirty-two. You moved one, I moved one. That's how it works.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face. And take this, a little present from me: Plaza del Dos de Mayo.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Two from you, two from me. 94 P. We can do this all night, amigo.

Ay, hijo, listen to me now. You repeat the same words like a little parrot, hoping Abuela gets tired. I do not get tired, and I do not forget my own table. Taxi Blanco, ten P — that is my word. Sí or no, cariño?
Two primas you moved. I move one. Ninety-six. Card's not getting cheaper.

¡Ay, qué bueno eres, hijo! But my purse does not grow, verdad? For the Taxi Blanco, 5. Still 5, cariño. Forty years this table, and always small coins. If you like, El Chato next door has better packs. Now tell me, have you eaten something today?

Ay, hijo, you are patient like my late husband. Mira — 24 P, and I put it in a little sleeve so the corners stay perfect. Twenty-nine was my price this morning, and look at me now! Eat something, cariño, the bread is here.
Lista vieja. Hoy son noventa y siete. Pago al momento también me gusta, pero el precio no baja por eso. ¿Lo quieres o no?
